headline: We grow the numbers behind the harvest.
deck: A field seen from three distances. Read the signals from orbit, follow the water, and move in close enough to see a single leaf.

image.alt: Circular irrigated fields and cloud shadows seen from above.

readings.label: Soil moisture
readings.title: Beneath the surface
readings.body: Moisture is one part of this field’s story. Soil texture, sensor depth and the stage of the crop give the reading its meaning.

readings.label: NDVI
readings.title: Across the field
readings.body: Vegetation reflects red and near-infrared light differently. NDVI compares the two. A change across the field gives a grower somewhere to look more closely.

readings.label: Canopy temperature
readings.title: Within the canopy
readings.body: Leaves experience a microclimate of their own. Canopy temperature adds context when read alongside soil moisture and conditions on the ground.

chapters.title: From orbit to earth.
chapters.body: At ground level, circles on the satellite image become rows of crops and the reach of an irrigation arm. Field observations give the view from above its context.

image.alt: A center-pivot irrigation arm crosses green crop rows in front of distant mountains.

chapters.title: Small beginnings.
chapters.body: Light catches the edge of a young leaf. What a plant can become starts with its genetics. Soil, weather and the growing season shape how that potential appears in the field.

image.alt: Beads of water sit on a softly backlit green leaf.

chapters.title: The shape of a season.
chapters.body: From above, a field becomes part of a larger pattern. Reading water, vegetation and temperature together gives a single observation a place in the season.

image.alt: Clouds drift across contrasting circular farms in a dry landscape.
